_comment: The committed import allowlist of the sandboxes.
app_spec.xml, Untrusted Code Sandbox, feature 167:
System rejects a submitted module importing anything outside the
configured allowlist, which returns a disallowed_import error message
(docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md 5.2: 'LLM-authored code is untrusted
code. Treat it that way.'; 10.2: the policy runtime blocks 'any import
outside an allowlist'; 11.1: 'no imports outside the allowlist' among
the static checks before a policy is admitted; 12's determinism row:
'time, datetime.now, random without seed blocked by the import
allowlist').
The compile in packages/sandbox/src/sandbox/imports.py refuses this
file and any change to it that is not a list of well-formed dotted
module terms - so the ceiling below is not a convention the next edit
can forget: it is the configuration, checked, and a submitted module
importing a term it does not cover is refused with the code
disallowed_import.
What the ceiling covers, and why each term earns its place:
- the deterministic stdlib working set (math, decimal, fractions,
statistics, itertools, functools) - the same six feature 139's
committed default carries, the arithmetic a signal needs;
- datetime and random, both present because the deterministic
spellings need the modules: a datetime built from explicit
arguments is a value, and the seeded RNG of section 12's next row
('seed passed into signal(); stored on the node') is
random.Random(seed). The clock constructors inside them
(datetime.now, unseeded draws) are policed at the search seam by
feature 139's floor; time itself is ABSENT here because it has no
sanctioned spelling - every use of it is a wall-clock read;
- typing, collections, dataclasses - the structure of a deterministic
module, no I/O among them;
- __future__ - a compiler directive, not a module the box executes;
- polars, numpy, pyarrow - the payload stack: section 5.1's contract
is polars-native (bars() returns pl.DataFrame, signal returns
pl.Series), the numeric layer sits beneath it, and the window
arrives as Arrow IPC over the payload channel (5.2, feature 166).
Absent by design: os, sys, socket, subprocess, pathlib and every
other module that touches the world the box refuses (5.2's control
table: no network, no mounts) - a deployment widening this list is
narrowing the box, and the widen happens here, in review, or not at
all.
This is one allowlist for every box the isolation policy covers - the
feature's own sentence and section 10.2's both say 'the allowlist',
singular, and the two Z1 boxes of isolation_policy.json submit against
the same ceiling this file is.
